name: Bie
description: A star 171 parsecs away, 29 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 90982: radius 28.774 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 440.857 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.069) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 90982: effective temperature 4934 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.062)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 90982: distance 170.94 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.046), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 171 parsecs away, 29 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 441 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,934 K, so 28.774 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 90982: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Theta Coronae Australis
quotes.card: Theta Coronae Australis, also named Bie, is a solitary yellow-hued star located in the southern constellation of Corona Australis.
quotes.introduction: Its Bayer designation is Latinized from θ Coronae Australis, and abbreviated Theta CrA or θ CrA.
